Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values that Blizzard may revise. This is warlock-meta-blazing-scream rebuilt around the single quality-of-life theme running through the whole Warlock section of the 3.2.0 notes: Hellfire Aura, Dark Prison's Chain Aura and Bombardment's Endless Barrage all became castable while moving. Season 14 Warlock was a stand-still class with a ramp; three lines in one patch removed the stand-still half. This variant leans all the way into that by swapping the meta build's static trail-painting for a Sigil-heavy bar that keeps damage going out while you never stop, and by taking Sigil of Chaos so Dark Prison's Calamity - which is now also a Sigil Skill at 200% damage, up from 30% - is part of a coherent Sigil package rather than an isolated nuke. It trades some peak single-target for far better uptime in Challenge Dungeons and Overland Ambushes, the two new PTR activities that specifically punish standing still.

Rotation
  1. Keep Hellfire Aura maintained, open every pack with Dark Prison, Bombardment continuously while you walk, and Blazing Scream through the middle.
  2. The whole point is never losing a cast to repositioning, so keep moving.
Variants

Leveling — Keep moving. Hellfire Aura up while you walk, Blazing Scream across packs as you pass through them, Dread Claws on anything that survives. Wall of Agony only when something forces you to hold ground. The habit to build now is never stopping to cast - that is the whole point of the variant.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Elegy in hand - the same gate as the base build, because it is the same damage spine.

Early Endgame — Hellfire Aura on, then never stop walking. Dark Prison (Calamity) into the pack for the 200% hit, Bombardment while repositioning, Blazing Scream on the pass-through. Sigil of Smoke makes things Vulnerable on hit, which turns on Bane Link Aspect's +15% - so the Vulnerable application is now a damage step, not a debuff you can skip.
Move on when Infernal Homunculus equipped. Free Lesser Demon Upgrades at 200% duration matter more here than anywhere else, because a build that never stands still has no window to re-apply anything by hand.

Late Endgame — Full mobile loop: Hellfire Aura maintained, Dark Prison (Calamity) as the opener into every pack, Bombardment continuously while walking, Blazing Scream through the middle. Overwhelming Aspect's 7-17% per Overpower stack doubles against Hexed enemies, so Hex uptime is still a damage stat here even though the bar is different.
Move on when You are comfortably clearing Challenge Dungeons at one to two Torment tiers above your normal difficulty. That activity is the reason this variant exists - it scales up to three tiers above and does not let you stand still.

Pushing — Accept the trade honestly: this variant gives up the base build's peak burst - the Eightfold Idol trail stacking on an anchored pack - in exchange for never losing a cast to repositioning. On corridor pushes where you are always moving, that is a gain; on a stationary boss, warlock-meta-blazing-scream is the better build and you should swap to it. Everything here describes 3.2.0 PTR behaviour and may change before Season 15 launches.

Uniques
  • weapon PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak, next to the main Waypoint in any major city - his boosts include random uniques. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; re-verify against the launch notes. Still mandatory here: without Elegy, Blazing Scream is not an Archfiend Skill and the whole damage spine is missing. Where →
  • offhand PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. Lower priority on this variant than on the base build - the trails matter less when you are not anchoring packs to a spot, so do not delay playing this variant waiting for it. Where →
  • chest PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. The 200%-longer free Lesser Demon Upgrades are worth more here than on the base build, because a mobile build has less time to re-apply anything. Where →
  • ring PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. 100-130% damage bonus on the PTR. Where →
  • amulet PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. 120-130% damage bonus on the PTR. Where →
  • helm Mythic Unique, all classes. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: craft at the Jeweler from Resplendent Sparks and Runes selecting the helm slot - on 3.2.0 the Jeweler route carries no Crafted tag, so it does not spend your one crafted-Mythic slot; alternatively a Blacksmith Mythic cache, or any boss drop. Where →
  • SSplinter of Anguish jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. Same reasoning as the base build - Splinter of Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance is disqualifying for any crit-scaling Warlock. Budget extra Dominance Regeneration to cover Anguish's +30% Primary Resource cost, which hurts more on this higher-cast-rate variant. Where →

Point allocation, in order60 points across 6 nodes

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build on any site - the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides on 2026-08-08, day 5 of the 8-day PTR. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list the PTR digest authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build. Warlock is the thinnest case of the three PTR classes: no Warlock upgrade-mod names were published anywhere consulted, so this records skills and point counts only. The one build-level artefact found anywhere for 3.2.0 Warlock was a Korean Inven post whose allocation is an encoded string that could not be decoded - so nothing was taken from it.

Skill point priority

  1. Blazing Scream to max - identical to the base build, and for the same reason
  2. Sigil of Chaos early rather than late: Hellfire Aura is castable while moving on the PTR, which is a bigger practical gain while levelling than any damage number on this list
  3. Dread Claws for Ravenous Jaws' 500% Eviscerate damage
  4. Wall of Agony (Encircle) while the Dominance pool is small
  5. Command Fallen (Fallen Rush) for bodies between packs
  6. Apocalypse as the ultimate

Warlock is the thinnest case of the three PTR classes: no Warlock upgrade-mod names were published anywhere consulted, so this records skills and point counts only. The one build-level artefact found anywhere for 3.2.0 Warlock was a Korean Inven post whose allocation is an encoded string that could not be decoded - so nothing was taken from it.

Skill point priority

  1. Everything maxed on Blazing Scream, Dark Prison, Bombardment and Sigil of Chaos
  2. Defensive passives over the last damage nodes
  3. Do not chase Control glyph here - without Umbral Chains you cannot reach its 30% band and the 15% band is not worth a slot at push tiers

Board & glyph focus

Not open yet. Bank the points. Note the divergence from the base build already starts here: Dominance Regeneration is a first-class stat on this variant from level one, because you cast more.

Board & glyph focus

Superiority glyph first - its +2.0% Dominance Regeneration is worth more on this variant than the +30% to magic nodes, which is not something you can say about the base build. Occultist second. Control glyph only for the 15% Slowed/Taunted band, and only if you have a spare slot.

Board & glyph focus

Superiority and Occultist maxed, then magic-node boards. Same gearing note as the base build: on 3.2.0 the Jeweler's rune-crafted Mythics carry no Crafted tag, so the Season 14 one-crafted-Mythic ceiling does not bind and you can wear Harlequin Crest without spending your craft.

Board & glyph focus

Fully min-maxed magic-node routes under Superiority, held to whatever Dominance Regeneration floor stops you stalling mid-corridor. Take Diabolic Armor's 10-15% and Scorn's flat 15% Damage Reduction over a last damage node - both were handed out free in 3.2.0 and this variant eats more incidental damage than the base build by design.

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries - not one mercenary name appears in the official 3.2.0 notes. This is the Season 14 Blazing Scream guidance carried over, and it is worth being honest that the source is thinner here than for Barbarian or Rogue: Maxroll's Season 14 Blazing Scream guide offers Varyana for sustain or Raheir's Bastion for survivability without settling on one. The choice recorded here is the specialist's - Raheir hired for Valiance's cheat-death, because a Warlock that has to ramp its damage cannot afford to die mid-ramp, with Varyana reinforcing on Bloodthirst. If you test this and find the ramp is never the problem, invert it. Bloodthirst's attack speed is worth more on this variant than on the base build, since the whole point here is casting more often while moving.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values that Blizzard may revise. This is warlock-meta-blazing-scream rebuilt around the single quality-of-life theme running through the whole Warlock section of the 3.2.0 notes: Hellfire Aura, Dark Prison's Chain Aura and Bombardment's Endless Barrage all became castable while moving. Season 14 Warlock was a stand-still class with a ramp; three lines in one patch removed the stand-still half. This variant leans all the way into that by swapping the meta build's static trail-painting for a Sigil-heavy bar that keeps damage going out while you never stop, and by taking Sigil of Chaos so Dark Prison's Calamity - which is now also a Sigil Skill at 200% damage, up from 30% - is part of a coherent Sigil package rather than an isolated nuke. It trades some peak single-target for far better uptime in Challenge Dungeons and Overland Ambushes, the two new PTR activities that specifically punish standing still.

Rotation
  1. Keep Hellfire Aura maintained, open every pack with Dark Prison, Bombardment continuously while you walk, and Blazing Scream through the middle.
  2. The whole point is never losing a cast to repositioning, so keep moving.
Variants

Leveling — Keep moving. Hellfire Aura up while you walk, Blazing Scream across packs as you pass through them, Dread Claws on anything that survives. Wall of Agony only when something forces you to hold ground. The habit to build now is never stopping to cast - that is the whole point of the variant.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Elegy in hand - the same gate as the base build, because it is the same damage spine.

Early Endgame — Hellfire Aura on, then never stop walking. Dark Prison (Calamity) into the pack for the 200% hit, Bombardment while repositioning, Blazing Scream on the pass-through. Sigil of Smoke makes things Vulnerable on hit, which turns on Bane Link Aspect's +15% - so the Vulnerable application is now a damage step, not a debuff you can skip.
Move on when Infernal Homunculus equipped. Free Lesser Demon Upgrades at 200% duration matter more here than anywhere else, because a build that never stands still has no window to re-apply anything by hand.

Late Endgame — Full mobile loop: Hellfire Aura maintained, Dark Prison (Calamity) as the opener into every pack, Bombardment continuously while walking, Blazing Scream through the middle. Overwhelming Aspect's 7-17% per Overpower stack doubles against Hexed enemies, so Hex uptime is still a damage stat here even though the bar is different.
Move on when You are comfortably clearing Challenge Dungeons at one to two Torment tiers above your normal difficulty. That activity is the reason this variant exists - it scales up to three tiers above and does not let you stand still.

Pushing — Accept the trade honestly: this variant gives up the base build's peak burst - the Eightfold Idol trail stacking on an anchored pack - in exchange for never losing a cast to repositioning. On corridor pushes where you are always moving, that is a gain; on a stationary boss, warlock-meta-blazing-scream is the better build and you should swap to it. Everything here describes 3.2.0 PTR behaviour and may change before Season 15 launches.

Same reasoning as the base build - Splinter of Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance is disqualifying for any crit-scaling Warlock. Budget extra Dominance Regeneration to cover Anguish's +30% Primary Resource cost, which hurts more on this higher-cast-rate variant. Where →

Reasoning

Based onElegy Blazing Scream Warlock
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. Bar swap: Umbral Chains out, Sigil of Chaos in. The meta build uses Umbral Chains to pull packs to a fixed spot so the Eightfold Idol trails land where enemies will be; this variant never stands at a fixed spot, so the pull is dead weight. Sigil of Chaos brings Hellfire Aura (castable while moving on the PTR) and Sigil of Smoke (makes enemies Vulnerable on hit), which feeds Bane Link Aspect's +15% damage to Vulnerable enemies.
  2. Dark Prison is played for Calamity rather than for Chain Aura's control. Calamity went 30% to 200% damage on the PTR and became a Sigil Skill, so on this bar it counts for both the damage and the Sigil package - the meta build treats it as a lock-down tool instead.
  3. Aspect swap: Enfeebling Aspect out, Misfortune Aspect in on the amulet. Enfeebling's Weaken rider matters when you hold a pack in place; Misfortune's flat 15% reduction from Hexed enemies is unconditional and this variant takes more incidental hits because it fights while repositioning.
  4. Aspect swap: Nefarious Aspect out, Cauterization Aspect in on the boots. Nefarious converts direct damage to Shadow while in Shadowform, which pairs with the meta build's trail stacking; Cauterization converts to Fire while Volatile and adds a 40% chance to Fortify 3-6% Maximum Life, which is the survivability this variant needs when it is inside packs rather than behind trails.
  5. Paragon reweighting: Control glyph is taken for its 15% against Slowed/Taunted rather than its 30% against Tethered/Knocked Down, because dropping Umbral Chains removes the Tether source. This is a real downgrade and is accepted deliberately - do not take Control glyph at all if you are short on glyph slots.
  6. Soul Splinter unchanged: Splinter of Anguish, not Hellfire. Both builds scale with critical strikes, so Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance is disqualifying for both. Anguish's +30% Primary Resource cost bites harder here because this variant casts more often - budget more Dominance regeneration on boots and helm to pay for it.
  7. Gear: The Eightfold Idol stays but drops in priority. Its Shadow and Lava trails are worth less to a build that does not control where enemies walk. If you have not found it, this variant is playable without it, which the meta build genuinely is not.
